name: Gross Rental Yield
description: Computes gross rental yield as annual rental income divided by the property purchase price, times 100. It is a simple, unadjusted measure of a rental property's income return.
notes: This ignores operating expenses, vacancy, and financing costs; use net rental yield for a more complete picture. Income and price must be in the same currency.

name: Net Rental Yield
description: Subtracts annual operating expenses from annual rental income, divides by the property price, and multiplies by 100 to give net rental yield. It reflects the return after the costs of running the property.
notes: Operating expenses typically include maintenance, insurance, management fees, and taxes, but not mortgage interest. All figures must share the same currency and period.

name: Rent rule of thumb
description: Applies the common guideline that rent should not exceed about 30% of income, returning 30% of monthly income as a suggested rent ceiling.
notes: This is a general benchmark, not a strict limit; affordable rent depends on other expenses, debts, and local costs. Some guidelines use gross and others net income.

name: Net Operating Income (NOI)
description: Gives a property's income after vacancy and operating costs but before debt service and income tax.
notes: Operating expenses exclude mortgage payments, depreciation and capital improvements.

name: Capitalisation Rate
description: Divides net operating income by value: the unlevered yield of an income property.
notes: Lower cap rates mean higher prices relative to income.

name: Value by Direct Capitalisation
description: Estimates a property's value by dividing its stable NOI by the market capitalisation rate.
notes: Small changes in the cap rate move the value a lot: 6 % instead of 5 % takes one sixth off.

name: Gross Rent Multiplier
description: Divides price by gross yearly rent, a quick screening ratio.
notes: Ignores expenses, so compare only similar properties.

name: Cash-on-Cash Return
description: Divides the yearly pre-tax cash flow after debt service by the cash invested.
notes: Ignores appreciation and principal paid down.

name: Break-even Occupancy Ratio
description: Gives the occupancy needed to cover operating costs and debt service.
notes: Lenders like to see it below about 85 %.

name: Debt Yield
description: Divides NOI by the loan amount: the return the lender would earn if it had to take over the property.
notes: Commercial lenders often require at least 8–10 %.

name: Operating Expense Ratio
description: Divides operating expenses by effective gross income.

name: Mortgage Constant
description: Gives the yearly debt service per unit of loan for a monthly-pay amortising loan.
notes: Multiply by the loan amount for the yearly payments; compare with the cap rate for positive leverage.

name: Equity Multiple
description: Divides all cash returned to investors (including sale proceeds) by the equity invested.
notes: Ignores timing; pair it with the IRR.

name: One Percent Rule Check
description: Gives monthly rent as a percentage of price; the rule of thumb says a rental should reach about 1 %.
notes: A crude filter only; it ignores expenses, taxes and location.

name: Property Tax from a Mill Rate
description: Gives property tax when the rate is quoted in mills (currency units per 1000 of assessed value).
notes: A mill rate of 15 is a 1.5 % tax on assessed value.

name: Affordable Rent (30 % Rule)
description: Gives the monthly rent that keeps housing costs within a share of gross income.
notes: Households spending more than 30 % are usually considered cost-burdened.

name: Price-to-Rent Ratio

variables.label: Monthly rent of a similar home

description: Divides a home's price by a year of rent for a similar home.
notes: Above about 20 renting tends to be cheaper than buying; below about 15 buying tends to win.

name: Stamp-Duty-Style Tiered Tax
expression: sum(k, 1, len(th), max(min(price, at(th, k) + 0 * k) - if(k == 1, 0, at(th, k - 1)), 0) * at(rt, k))
description: Applies a tiered (slice) tax: each band of the price is taxed at its own rate, as in many property-transfer taxes.
notes: Enter your own bands and rates; the defaults are only an illustration.
